PLACED HERE WITH RESERVATION: the street matches this household, but the age does not. This man is 32 in December 1816; the Giuseppe of strada Camellara is 36 in June 1818, which would make him 34 here. The trade differs too — massaro di campagna against contadino. It may be the same man loosely aged, or a third Giuseppe.
«figlia delli fu Giuseppe Falco» — dead by July 1817. A Falco head of the founding generation, distinct from every Giuseppe Falco so far recorded: the others are alive in 1816 and 1818.
«e Rosa Sossi» — «delli fu» governs both parents, so she too was dead by July 1817. The Sossi are one of the largest families in the 1817 register.
«Maria Falco figlia delli fu Giuseppe Falco e Rosa Sossi, vedova di Francesco Quotolo» — died at twelve o'clock. No age is given; the 1816–18 form does not ask for one.

Aged 65, so born about 1752 — the oldest man this archive has placed in a Falco household's orbit.

«figlio di Giuseppe di Guida» — no «fu». Declares twice in three weeks and the ages do not match: «di anni trentanove, contadino» on 28 September, «di anni trentatre, massaro di campagna» on 21 October. Almost certainly one man loosely aged rather than two. HE IS NOT the Francesco Quotolo who married Maria Falco — that one was already dead by July 1817.

«Raffaele Falco figlio di Vincenzo Falco, e d'Andreana Crisci» — died at seven in the morning, aged about eighteen months. THIS IS THE BURIAL OF THE FIRST RAFFAELE, born 25 April 1816, and it settles generation four: the Raffaele of 10 May 1818 is the one who lived. Declared by Sabato Vassallo, 26, sportellaro of strada Porta di Sopra, and by GIUSEPPE FALCO, 37, massaro di campagna of strada Camellara, the two of them «PARENTI» — kin.

«Giuseppe Falco, di anni trentasette, di professione massaro di campagna, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Camellara» — twice in five days: on 24 October for a neighbour, Marianna Petrillo, and on 28 October for Vincenzo Falco's infant son Raffaele, where he and Sabato Vassallo are called «PARENTI». Vincenzo is a grandson of Matteo; Giuseppe is a documented son of Matteo, which would make him Vincenzo's uncle — and the register's own word for the relationship is kin. Aged 37 here, so born about 1780.
«figlia delli fu Nicola Majone» — dead by February 1818. NOT the Nicola Majone whose wife was Maria Casella and whose son Giovanni died 9 July 1817; that is a different couple in the same register.

«e Maria Falco» — «delli fu» governs both parents, so she too was dead by February 1818. A FALCO WOMAN MARRIED INTO THE MAJONE. Whether she is the Maria Falco buried on 24 July 1817 — «figlia delli fu Giuseppe Falco e Rosa Sossi, vedova di Francesco Quotolo» — is NOT established. One woman twice widowed would fit the dates; so would two women of the same name. Nothing here decides it.

«Angela, seu Lella Majone, figlia delli fu Nicola Majone, e Maria Falco, moglie di Giuseppe Sossi» — died at nineteen hours. «seu» = «or», the register giving both the formal name and the one she was called by.
«moglie di Giuseppe Sossi» — alive in February 1818, no age given
the act naming this marriage is her own death act

«e di Giuseppe Falco, di anni trentasei, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Camellara» — declaring the death of a neighbour, Emanuela d'Onofrio, with Domenico Balletta, 40, sartore, of the same street. THIS IS THE SIGHTING THAT TIES THE OTHERS TOGETHER: one month later, on 7 June 1818, the birth act of his daughter Maddalena gives him as thirty-six, contadino, of strada Camellara, husband of Antonia di Guida. Same age, same trade, same street, four weeks apart — one man, not two. Balletta is his neighbour in October 1817 as well.
«figlio di Giuseppe Morgillo» — no «fu». WEAK INFERENCE ONLY — see the corrections page on «quondam», 14 Sep 2026
«e Gelsomina Rivetti» — a THIRD Morgillo–Rivetti marriage: the two families the Falco married also married each other
«Pasquale Morgillo figlio di Giuseppe Morgillo, e Gelsomina Rivetti» — died at ten in the morning; no age given

«e di Orazio Morgillo, di anni ventisei, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Travo» — born about 1792. A LEAD, NOT A LINK: generation four's wife, Angela Rosa Morgillo, is recorded as a daughter of an ORAZIO Morgillo and was born 24 February 1818 — when a man of this age would have been twenty-six. But she was born at SAN FELICE, not Arienzo, and Orazio is not rare enough to assume. This is the first Orazio Morgillo this archive has met in any record.
«Angelo Morgillo FU Simone» — the register distinguishes him by his dead father, so Simone Morgillo was gone by July 1818
«Angelo Morgillo fu Simone, di anni cinquanta, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Travo» — born about 1768

«figlia delli fu Carlantonio Morgillo» — dead by August 1818. A SECOND Carlantonio Morgillo, and the discovery matters: the Carlantonio Morgillo who married Rosa Falco was alive in 1830, and declares this very act aged thirty-three. Two men of the name, one generation apart.
«e Manilia Rivetti» — «delli fu» governs both. A fourth Morgillo–Rivetti marriage in these registers.
«Giuditta Morgillo figlia delli fu Carlantonio Morgillo, e Manilia Rivetti, vedova di Giuseppe Gimbardo» — died at sixteen hours

«Carlantonio Morgillo, di anni trentatre, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Maddalena» — declaring the death of GIUDITTA MORGILLO as «vicino, parente», with Matteo Migliore of San Felice. A FOURTH sighting, and it tightens the age: thirty-three in September 1817 and thirty-three again in August 1818, against thirty in February 1816 and thirty-six in October 1816. The two later readings agree on a birth about 1784–85. AND A LEAD: Giuditta is daughter of the LATE Carlantonio Morgillo and Manilia Rivetti, and this Carlantonio declares her death as kin. He is very plausibly her brother, which would give this man's own parents. The act says «parente» without saying how, so it is not asserted.

«sono comparsi D. Giuseppe Rivetti, di anni quarantuno, di professione SACERDOTE, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Sant'Andrea» — a Rivetti priest, born about 1777. With the Donna Francesca Rivetti of January 1816, daughter of Don Nicola Rivetti and Donn'Anna Quotolo, he is the second sign of a Rivetti branch of standing at Arienzo. He is recorded as a household of one because a priest has no wife; «father» is only the schema's word for a head.

«Angelandrea Rivetti figlia del fu Crescenzo Rivetti, ed Angela Falco» — died at eight in the morning, two years and two months after her father. THE FIRST CHILD OF THIS MARRIAGE TO BE FOUND, and the second record anywhere to name Angela Falco. Declared by Arcangelo Anigale, 48, fruttajolo, and Raffaele Rivetti, 26, contadino, as «vicino e parente». Angela is named without «fu», so she was still living in February 1819.

«Domenico Falco figlio di Giuseppe Falco, e Gelsomina Vigliotta» — died at twelve o'clock, aged about two years and four months; he was born 25 November 1816. Declared by Francesco Martone, cantiniere, and Michele Bordica, 27, contadino, both «nella Camellara, vicini».

«Rosaria Falco figlia di Giuseppe Falco, e Gelsomina Vigliotta» — died at twenty-three hours THE SAME DAY as her brother Domenico, eleven hours after him. No birth act has been found for her: she is not in the Arienzo birth registers of 1816, 1817 or 1818, so she was born earlier. Declared by a neighbour of strada Sossi and Francesco Martone, 47, cantiniere, of strada Camellara.

«Angelo Quotolo figlio di Francesco Quotolo, e Vittoria di Guida» — died at eleven

«e di Giuseppe di Guida, di anni sessantotto, di professione massaro di campagna, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Maddalena» — born about 1751. A LEAD: a Giuseppe di Guida is named in October 1817 as the father of Angelo Andrea di Guida by Michedalena Rivetti, and Giuseppe Falco of strada Camellara married an ANTONIA DI GUIDA. A man of sixty-eight in 1819 is the right age to be father to both. Nothing here names Antonia, so it is not asserted.

«Carlantonio Morgillo, di anni trentacinque, contadino» — a FIFTH sighting. Thirty-three in August 1818 and thirty-five fourteen months later: fast by a year, but the run 33 (Sept 1817), 33 (Aug 1818), 35 (Oct 1819) is broadly consistent and keeps the birth around 1784-85. The outliers remain the two 1816 readings, thirty and thirty-six.

«figlio di ARCANGELO CRISCI, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara» — the FIRST CIVIL RECORD to place this marriage on the ground. Until now the archive knew of Arcangelo Crisci's marriage to Anna Falco only at second hand. He is a contadino, and he lives on the family's own street.

«e di ANNA FALCO, domiciliata ivi» — alive on 24 January 1820, and bearing a child two days earlier. She is said to have died at twenty-two later in this same year, which would put her birth about 1798.

«è morto nella sua propria casa FORTUNATO CRISCI di giorni due, nato in Arienzo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara» — two days old. Declared by ANDREA CRISCI, 60, and MARCELLO CRISCI, 25, both contadini of strada Camellara, each «vicino del defunto». The Andrea Crisci who reported Anna Falco's namesake's death in 1831 is given as fifty-eight, which fits this man.

«è morta nella sua propria casa ANNA FALCO di anni venticinque, moglie di ARCANGELO CRISCI, nata in Arienzo, di professione Contadina, domiciliata ivi strada Camellara, FIGLIA DI PASQUALE FALCO, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, E DI CHIARA RIVETTI, domiciliata ivi» — atto 47. A DAUGHTER OF THE DIRECT LINE'S GENERATION TWO, and a sister of Vincenzo Falco. Aged twenty-five, so born about 1795. She had buried a two-day-old son, Fortunato Crisci, seven months earlier.

On his daughter Anna's death act he is «PASQUALE FALCO, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara» — WITHOUT «fu» or «defunto». So he was alive on 23 August 1820, a contadino, living on strada Camellara, fourteen years before his own death act of 1 October 1834. This is an independent civil sighting of the ancestor between his marriage and his death.

«e di CHIARA RIVETTI, domiciliata ivi» — named without «fu» on her daughter Anna's death act, so alive in August 1820 and living on strada Camellara. Until now the only record naming her at all was her own Latin burial entry of 1843.

«figlio di NICOLA RIVETTI Defunto, di professione Contadino» — a CONTADINO Nicola Rivetti, dead by September 1821. THE BEST CANDIDATE YET FOR CHIARA RIVETTI'S FATHER: Chiara, who married Pasquale Falco, is «filia quondam NICOLAI et ANNA» in her 1843 Latin burial entry and was born about 1763; this Nicola's son Carmine was born about 1768. Same forename, same generation, and the same station — Chiara married a contadino.

«e di ANNA DI RUGGIO Defunta» — IF this is Chiara Rivetti's mother, then the «Anna» of the 1843 entry was ANNA DI RUGGIO, and the Rivetti of this line were contadini, not the Don Nicola / Donn'Anna Quotolo house of the 1816 lead. Not established.

«CARMINE RIVETTI di anni cinquantatre, marito di GIUSTINA MORGILLO, nato in Arienzo, di professione Contadino» — born about 1768. Declared by Marcello Rivetti, 36, of the same street, and Giovanni Morgillo fu Raffaele, 45, «parente del defunto».
«marito di Giustina Morgillo»
named as his wife — another Morgillo–Rivetti marriage

«è morta nella sua propria casa ANGELA FALCO di anni CINQUANTUNO, VEDOVA DI CRESCENZO RIVETTI, nata in Arienzo, di professione Contadina, domiciliata ivi strada Capodiuomo, FIGLIA DI MATTEO FALCO Defunto, di professione Contadino, E DI FRANCESCA CRISCI Defunta» — atto 65. A DAUGHTER OF THE FOUNDING COUPLE, and so a sister of Pasquale. Aged fifty-one, so born about 1771. This is the THIRD time Matteo Falco and Francesca Crisci are named from a child's death act, and the EARLIEST of the three — before Rosa's of 1830 and Pasquale's of 1834.

«ANGELA FALCO di anni cinquantuno, vedova di CRESCENZO RIVETTI … figlia di MATTEO FALCO Defunto … e di FRANCESCA CRISCI Defunta» — she outlived Crescenzo by nearly six years and had moved from strada Camellara to strada Capodiuomo. Declared by Nicola Maggione and Alessandro Martone, both twenty-two and both «vicino della defunta». HER PARENTAGE EXPLAINS THE 1816 ACT: when Crescenzo died, GIOACCHINO FALCO and GIUSEPPE FALCO declared it as «parenti del defunto» — they were his wife's brothers.

«e GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, di anni quarantatre, di professione Contadino, regnicolo, domiciliato strada Camellara» — THE FIRST CIVIL RECORD TO STATE HIS PARENTAGE OUTRIGHT. The clerk adds «fu Matteo» to tell him from the other Giuseppe Falco of the town, and in doing so confirms from the civil series what the archive previously had only from the parish books: this Giuseppe is a son of the late Matteo Falco. Forty-three here, so born about 1780 — which agrees with the thirty-seven he gives in October 1817. He declares with Cesare Giglio, 50, of the same street, at the death of Maria Crisci, three years old, daughter of Marcello Crisci and Maria Rosa Mauro.

«figlia di MARCELLO CRISCI, di professione contadino» — the Marcello Crisci, 25, who declared the death of Fortunato Crisci, son of Arcangelo Crisci and Anna Falco, on strada Camellara in January 1820
«e di MARIA ROSA MAURO, domiciliata ivi»
«MARIA CRISCI, di anni tre, nata in Arienzo, di professione contadina» — declared by Cesare Giglio and GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, both of strada Camellara
«figlia di FRANCESCO COSSI, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi» — named without «fu», so living

«e di MARIA FALCO, domiciliata ivi» — A LIVING MARIA FALCO in 1823, and therefore a third woman of the name. She is not the Maria Falco buried on 24 July 1817 (daughter of Giuseppe Falco and Rosa Sossi, widow of Francesco Quotolo), nor the Maria Falco who was already dead in February 1818 as the mother of Angela Majone. Her own parents are not named here. The declarant is GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, who gives himself as a «vicino» and not as kin — so nothing in the act joins her to the line.
«ANTONIA COSSI, di mesi nove, nata in Arienzo» — atto 39, died at fifteen hours

«sono comparsi GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, di anni quarantadue, di professione Contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Sant'Andrea, vicino della defunta» — atto 39, the SECOND «fu Matteo» sighting in two days, at the death of Antonia Cossi, nine months old, daughter of Francesco Cossi and a MARIA FALCO. And he is given here on STRADA SANT'ANDREA where the day before he is on strada Camellara: in this form a declarant described as «vicino» is recorded at the street of the house where the death happened, so a declarant's street is NOT reliable evidence of where he himself lived.

THE ONLY RECORD IN WHICH PASQUALE FALCO ACTS FOR HIMSELF. Every other sighting has him named by somebody else: on his children's acts, or on his own death act of 1834. Here he walks into the town hall with his brother Giuseppe and reports a neighbour's child dead. He is fifty-five, which against his baptism of 24 October 1767 is one year out — ordinary. And his trade is given as COLONO, a tenant farmer, where his death act of 1834 calls him contadino.

«e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni quarantadue, di professione colono, regnicolo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, vicino del defunto» — declaring beside his brother PASQUALE FALCO. The only act found so far in which the two brothers appear together, and the first to give Giuseppe's trade as colono rather than contadino. Forty-two here, so born about 1782.

THE SURNAME IS AMBIGUOUS IN THE HAND: it can be read Cossi or Crisci, and the 1823 act was read Cossi. Recorded as Cossi with the doubt stated. Francesco Cossi and Maria Falco lost Antonia in June 1823, Giuseppe in March 1824 and Giuseppa here in April 1825, and Giuseppe Falco declared every one. The register calls him «vicino» each time and never «parente», so nothing states a relationship — but three appearances for one household is a pattern, and it is the best hint yet that this Maria Falco is his kin. His trade drifts again: contadino in 1823, colono in 1824, MASSARO here; and his age goes backwards, forty here against forty-two the year before.

«GIUSEPPA COSSI, di mesi otto, nata in Arienzo, di professione contadina, figlia di FRANCESCO COSSI, di professione Contadino, e di MARIA FALCO» — the third child of this house to die in three years, all three declared by GIUSEPPE FALCO of strada Camellara.

THIS CLOSES A LIFE THE ARCHIVE HAD ONLY OPENED: her civil birth act of 7 June 1818 records her born on strada Camellara to Giuseppe, thirty-six, and Antonia, and she died a week short of her seventh birthday. evidence: GENERATION FIVE. Son of Raffaele Falco and Angela Rosa Morgillo. MARRIED GIOVANNA ARRICALE ON 18 NOVEMBER 1872 AT ARIENZO — the date, not just the year. Named in both documents as the mother — «e figlia di ARRICALE GIOVANNA, contadina». HER PARENTS ARE READ FROM THE IMAGE: FRANCESCO ARRICALE, 24, contadino, and PASQUA FALCO, 25, both of STRADA CAPODICONCA, in her own birth act — atto 114 of 1848, born 22 December 1848. HER MOTHER WAS A FALCO — so generation five's groom and his bride's mother shared a surname. NO KINSHIP IS CLAIMED: Arienzo holds several Pasqua Falco in these years, mothers of Maione, Majone and Loffredo children among others, and this one is not identified beyond the act. HER SIBLINGS ARE NOT FINDABLE and the index is the reason: the Caserta collection covering 1809-1866 holds 1,086 Falco records for Arienzo and effectively NO Arricale at all, so it cannot show children of this couple. Use the full-text page transcripts for Arricale, not the name index The Arricale of Arienzo are a large and steady family of VATICALI — carriers — chiefly of strada Capodiconca, and the spelling wanders between Arricale, Arrigale and Arricole in the same decade and sometimes the same hand

DECLARED THE NEXT DAY BY THE MIDWIFE, «GELSOMINA RUGGIERO, di anni SESSANTA, di professione LEVATRICE, domiciliata in questo comune STRADA PORTA DI SOPRA» — a Gelsomina Ruggiero stood MATRINA at this couple's son Raffaele's baptism in 1818, and Andreana's own mother was a Ruggiero; NO KINSHIP IS CLAIMED, the name is common at Arienzo. Witnesses Pasquale Sansone, 38, contadino of strada Terra Murata, and Carlo Manna, 57, contadino of strada Camellara, both «asserito di non saper pure scrivere per non averlo mai imparato». Baptised at Sant'Andrea Apostolo, notamento returned 20 December. THE 1828 SCRIBE WRITES THE MOTHER'S SURNAME WITH A LIGATURE THIS READER COULD NOT SEPARATE FROM «CRISPI»; five other acts in this household give CRISCI, and the household is fixed by the husband and the street, not by the spelling

evidence: THE CIVIL BIRTH ACT OF DON GIOVANNI FALCO, THE DEACON — NOT A NEW CHILD. The archive already held his PARISH BAPTISM of 6 April 1825, read from the image on 14 Sep 2026; this is the same day from the other archive, and it was checked against what was held before it was written down. WHAT THE CIVIL ACT ADDS, and the baptism could not: he was BORN that same day «alle ore DICIASSETTE, nella casa sua propria di abitazione», strada Camellara, and his father declared him at TWENTY-ONE HOURS THE SAME EVENING. «…è comparso GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTACINQUE, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo comune STRADA CAMELLARA, quale ci ha presentato un MASCHIO … che lo stesso è nato da ANTONIA DI GUIDA sua moglie legitima, di anni QUARANTA … il nome di GIOVANNI». Witnesses Arcangelo Giglio, 22, FALEGNAME of strada Sant'Andrea, and Domenico Papa, 50, contadino of strada Camellara. Officer Giovan Battista de Baptistis, secondo eletto; parish Sant'Andrea Apostolo, notamento returned the same 6 April

evidence: «GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTACINQUE, di professione CONTADINO» — and «GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione MASSARO» on 2 APRIL 1825, FOUR DAYS EARLIER, in the same comune before the same office. FIVE YEARS IN FOUR DAYS, both read from the image. The strongest single demonstration this archive holds that a stated age in these registers is an estimate — no inference is needed, the contradiction is internal to one week of one year

THE DIGLIO ARE THE FALCO'S CAMELLARA NEIGHBOURS throughout this register: Aniello Diglio, 46, declared beside GIUSEPPE FALCO on 2 April 1825, and Cesare Diglio, 50, of strada Camellara witnessed this very act

evidence: «che la stessa è nata da MARIA FALCO sua moglie legitima, di anni TRENTATRE, domiciliata collo stesso» — A FOURTH MARIA FALCO, and the FIRST DOCUMENTED MARRIAGE TIE between a Falco woman and the Diglio. Thirty-three in May 1825 gives b. c.1792. SHE IS NOT the Maria Falco buried 24 July 1817 (daughter of Giuseppe Falco and Rosa Sossi, widow of Francesco Quotolo), NOR the Maria Falco already dead by February 1818 (wife of Nicola Majone), NOR the Maria Falco who was wife of FRANCESCO COSSI and living on 2 April 1825 — a woman cannot have two living husbands, and Francesco Cossi was alive that month. WHICH FALCO HOUSE SHE COMES FROM IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti baptised a Maria on 30 October 1790, which would make her thirty-four here rather than thirty-three; that is within this register's documented error, and it is NOT ENOUGH TO JOIN THEM

evidence: THE DATE OF A MARRIAGE THIS ARCHIVE HELD ONLY AS A FACT. The 1818 Tavola Alfabetica annuale de' Matrimonj pairs «ARCANGELO COSSI» with «ANNA FALCO», her parents given as «DI PASQUALE, e CHIARA RIVETTI» — no «fu» before either, and Pasquale Falco did not die until 1834. Married before the church 3 MAGGIO 1818. Anna was baptised 28 October 1795, so she married at TWENTY-TWO and was dead at twenty-four, on 23 August 1820. THE SURNAME IS WRITTEN COSSI HERE AND CRISCI IN THE 1820 ACTS — both read from the image, and this archive has already recorded that Cossi and Crisci are not reliably separable in this hand. The identification does not rest on it: there is one Anna Falco of Pasquale and Chiara, and one Arcangelo she was married to

evidence: THE FOURTH MARIA FALCO, IDENTIFIED — and the open question published about her yesterday is answered. «…è morta nella sua propria casa MARIA FALCO, d'anni TRENTADUE, MOGLIE DI ALFONSO DIGLIO, nata in Arienzo, di professione contadina, domiciliata ivi, FIGLIA DI PASQUALE FALCO, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, E DI CHIARA RIVETTI, domiciliata ivi» — atto 22, died at NINE in the morning in her own house. Declared by ANGELO SANSONE, 46, and TOMASO ESPOSITO, 50, both contadini of STRADA CAMELLARA and both «VICINO DELLA DEFUNTA» — neighbours, and the act says so rather than «parente». SHE IS ONE OF THE TWO MARIA FALCO BAPTISED TO THIS COUPLE, 13 September 1789 or 30 October 1790; WHICH ONE IS NOT SETTLED, and the stated age of thirty-two fits neither (it gives b. c.1794). The parentage is stated outright, so the identification does not depend on the number

evidence: SHE MARRIED HER FIRST COUSIN. «FALCO RAFFAELA | FALCO GIUSEPPE, e GUIDA ANTONIA» married «FALCO FRANCESCANTONIO | FALCO PASQUALE, e RIVETTI CHIARA» — and GIUSEPPE AND PASQUALE FALCO WERE BROTHERS, both sons of Matteo Falco. Born about 1820, she married at about TWELVE TO FOURTEEN by that reckoning, which is young enough to doubt: her death act of 20 April 1854 gives thirty-four, so b. c.1820, and the two figures cannot both be right. THE MARRIAGE IS READ FROM THE IMAGE; HER BIRTH YEAR IS NOT. Her brother Crescenzo's marriage act carries a papal dispensation «super quarto gradu consanguinitatis», so the house was marrying cousins in this generation as a matter of course

evidence: THE «FRANCESCO FALCO» OF THIS HOUSEHOLD IS FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO, SON OF PASQUALE FALCO AND CHIARA RIVETTI. The archive has carried this household since 13 September 2026 with the note that «her husband was also a Falco, which at Arienzo is common enough to prove nothing on its own». The 1832 marriage index proves it: same bride, same parents, and the groom's parentage stated. Their three recorded children — Carmina d. 19 Dec 1832, Clemente d. 14 Aug 1853, Pasqualina d. 14 Sep 1836 — are therefore GRANDCHILDREN OF MATTEO FALCO TWICE OVER, through both of his sons

evidence: AN UNATTACHED FALCO HOUSEHOLD, JOINED TO GENERATION FOUR. «10. FALCO MICHELANGELO | Arienzo | FALCO PASQUALE, e RIVETTI CHIARA» ed «VIGLIOTTI ANTONIA | Arienzo | VIGLIOTTI FRANCESCO, e REPETELLI VITTORIA | Xbre 1828» — the DAY is hidden behind the fold shadow in this filming, the month is unmistakable. This archive has carried «Michelangelo Falco (strada Camellara)» and «Michelangelo Falco & Mariantonia Vigliotta» as households with NO PARENTS FOR HIM. He is Pasquale Falco's son, and therefore VINCENZO FALCO'S BROTHER — which is why Vincenzo, 38, declared their daughter Anna's death on 4 May 1831 «come PARENTE della defunta». A relationship word the archive recorded in 1831 and could not explain until now

evidence: A NINTH CHILD, AND THE SECOND NECRONYM IN THIS HOUSEHOLD. «3. FALCO MATTEO | Arienzo | FALCO GIUSEPPE, e GUIDA ANTONIA | A 24 Gennajo 1834», his bride CRISCI ALESSANDRA. THE FIRST MATTEO — baptised 1807, named for his grandfather the founder — DIED 28 AUGUST 1809, so the name was given again to a later son, exactly as MADDALENA was given again in 1827 after the first Maddalena died in 1825. His bride's mother is written «[Quo]TOLO ANGELA», and ANIELLO CRISCI, who married this man's sister Giovanna in 1829, was son of «CRISCI CRESCENZO, e QUOTOLO ANGELA». THEY MAY BE BROTHER AND SISTER AND IT IS NOT CLAIMED: the father's forename here is obscured by the fold, and Angela Quotolo is not a rare name at Arienzo

evidence: THE ACT THAT LIFTS A REFUSAL THIS ARCHIVE MADE ON PURPOSE. «3. FALCO ANGELANDREA | Arienzo | FALCO VINCENZO, e CRISCI ANDREANA» ed «CIMMINO MARIA | Arienzo | CIMMINO ALESSANDRO, e SOLLI [ROSA]», the church date given as 24 MARZO [1847]. When Angelandrea's birth act of 12 September 1826 was published, it was DELIBERATELY NOT JOINED to «the ANGELO Falco who married Maria Cimmino in 1847 or the ANDREA Falco who married Maria Carmela», because the household held all three names and each of the other two was known only from a parish marriage act. THE CIVIL INDEX SETTLES ONE HALF: the man who married MARIA CIMMINO, daughter of Alessandro and Rosa Solli, is written ANGELANDREA — the exact name of the 1826 birth act — so ANGELO of the parish act and ANGELANDREA of the birth act are ONE MAN, married at TWENTY. The ANDREA who married Maria Carmela, daughter of Onofrio and Angela Imbimbo, REMAINS A SEPARATE SON and is still not joined to anything. DATE DISCREPANCY RECORDED, NOT RECONCILED: this tavola gives the church wedding as 24 March 1847 and the parish record held here gives 17 April 1847 — the same kind of civil-versus-parish disagreement already documented for Raffaele Falco's marriage of 1844

evidence: DATED AT LAST, AND THE BRIDE'S SURNAME SUPPLIED. «14. FALCO ANDREA | Arienzo | FALCO VINCENZO, e CRISCI ANDREANA» ed «BUONO MARIA CARMELA | Arienzo | BUONO ONOFRIO, ed IMBIMBO [ANGELA] | 24 MAGGIO 1846». The archive held this marriage from a Latin parish act with NO DATE and NO SURNAME for the bride — «Andream Falco Vincentii et Andreanae Crisci filium» m. «Maria Carmela, dau of Onofrio & Angela Imbimbo». Her family name is BUONO. AND IT SETTLES THE OTHER HALF OF THE ANGELO/ANDREA/ANGELANDREA TANGLE: Andrea married Maria Carmela Buono in MAY 1846 and Angelandrea married Maria Cimmino in MARCH 1847 — two men, two years, two wives, both sons of this house

evidence: A FOURTEEN-YEAR WINDOW CLOSED TO A DAY. «3. FALCO CRESCENZO | Arienzo | FALCO GIUSEPPE, e GUIDA [ANTONIA]» ed «MORGILLO ANGELA MARIA | Arienzo | MORGILLO GENNARO, e …» — 3 FEBRAJO 1845. The archive dated this marriage «c. 1831-46» from the parish act's papal dispensation «super quarto gradu consanguinitatis» granted by «Papa nostro GREGORIO» — Gregory XVI reigned 1831 to 1846, and that was the whole of the evidence. It is 3 February 1845, and the bride's father is GENNARO MORGILLO. THE DISPENSATION ITSELF IS NOT EXPLAINED BY THIS ENTRY: a fourth degree of consanguinity between a Falco of strada Camellara and a Morgillo is not yet traced

evidence: A CHILD FOR A HOUSEHOLD THAT HAD NONE. «ANGELO CRISCI ed ANNA RIVETTI | Arienzo | DI DOMENICO, e MARGARITA FALCO | A dì 29 NOVEMBRE [1819]» — his bride «Di Antonio, e Marchilia Auorolo». The archive holds MARGARITA FALCO, daughter of Francesco Falco and Maria Angela Ulivieccio, who died 13 May 1836 aged sixty as «moglie di DOMENICO CRISCI», and it holds her among the TWELVE PEOPLE IN THIS ARCHIVE WITH NO PARENT, NO SPOUSE, NO CHILD AND NO SIBLING attached. She has a son. AND SHE IS THE EARLIEST FALCO-CRISCI MARRIAGE FOUND: born about 1776, she married a Crisci a generation before Anna, Giovanna, Matteo and Francesca did

evidence: A FALCO FROM ANOTHER TOWN, RECORDED SO THAT NOBODY JOINS HIM BY MISTAKE. «20. FALCO FRANCESCO | AIROLA | FALCO PIETRO, e CARBONE […]» ed «RIVETTI GIUSEPPA | Arienzo | RIVETTI GIOVANNI, ed ALTARELLI […] | 23 AGOSTO 1848». His patria is AIROLA, not Arienzo, and his father PIETRO FALCO appears nowhere in this archive. NO KINSHIP TO THIS LINE IS CLAIMED OR SUSPECTED; he is here because the surname is the same and the archive's rule is that the surname identifies nobody

evidence: A FIFTH CHILD, AND THE ONE WHOSE TIMING MATTERS. «26. CLEMENTE COSSI, ed | Arienzo | Di CRISTOFARO, ed ORSOLA CARFORA» ed «ANGELA MARIA RIVETTI | Arienzo | Di [C]RESCENZO, ed ANGELA FALCO | A dì 26 NOVEMBRE 1816». HER FATHER DIED FIVE DAYS LATER, on 1 December 1816 — the act that Giuseppe Falco and Gioacchino Falco declared as «parenti», and the only record from which this archive knew the marriage existed at all. She married out of a house that was about to lose its head

evidence: THE MISSING MARRIAGE, FOUND. «13. ALFONSO DIGLIO | Arienzo | Di CESARE, ed ANNA MANNA» ed «MAGGIA FALCO | Arienzo | Di PASQUALE, e CHIARA RIVETTI | A 19 9bre 1813». THE BRIDE'S GIVEN NAME IS WRITTEN «MAGGIA» HERE and MARIA everywhere else — in her own death act of 25 April 1826, which names the same husband and the same two parents. The identification does not rest on the forename: one Alfonso Diglio, son of Cesare, one wife, one set of parents. The spelling is reported as found and NOT reconciled, the same treatment given to the Cossi/Crisci pair. She married at TWENTY-THREE or TWENTY-FOUR (baptised 1789 or 1790), bore Clementina in May 1825 and died eleven months later

evidence: «Di CESARE, ed ANNA MANNA» — CESARE DIGLIO, who witnessed his granddaughter Clementina's birth act in May 1825 aged fifty, and ANNA MANNA. THIS CORRECTS A READING PUBLISHED HERE YESTERDAY: the 1827 tavola entry for Alfonso's SECOND marriage was read as «Diglio Cesare, e M[anna] SARA», and the mother's forename was wrong. It is ANNA. The 1813 entry is the clearer hand and is twelve years closer to the fact

evidence: A FALCO HOUSEHOLD THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER SEEN. «8. LUIGI FALCO | Arienzo | Di SEBASTIANO, e COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO» ed «GIUSTINA PETRILLO | Arienzo | Fu SABATINO, e BRIGIDA COSSI | A 19 detto [1815]». NEITHER SEBASTIANO FALCO NOR COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THIS ARCHIVE — not in the households, not in the register, not in the people file. NOT THE LUIGI FALCO OF STRADA CAMELLARA, who was baptised in December 1819 to Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci and could not marry in 1815. NO KINSHIP TO THIS LINE IS CLAIMED. Recorded because the archive's standing position is that the surname identifies nobody, and the way to hold that position is to name the other houses rather than ignore them

evidence: A SECOND GIOVANNA FALCO OF THE FOUNDERS' GENERATION — OR THE SAME ONE, TWICE MARRIED, AND THE ARCHIVE DOES NOT SAY WHICH. «PASCALE LETTIERI | Arienzo | Fu AGOSTINO, e ROSA SPOSITO» ed «MARIA MICHELA MIGLIORE | Arienzo | DI GIUSEPPE, e GIOVANNA FALCO | A dì 14 GENNAJO [1819]». The «DI» before Giuseppe, where this scribe writes «FU» for the dead all down the same column, puts GIUSEPPE MIGLIORE ALIVE in January 1819. THE OTHER GIOVANNA FALCO in these indexes is the wife of ANTONIO LETTIERI of Paolisi, whose children married at Arienzo in 1826 and 1837. Two husbands. EITHER TWO WOMEN OF ONE NAME IN ONE GENERATION, OR ONE WOMAN WIDOWED AND REMARRIED BETWEEN 1819 AND 1826 — nothing read so far decides it, and neither is claimed. Note also that the groom here is a LETTIERI and so is the other Giovanna Falco's husband

evidence: GENERATION THREE'S OWN WEDDING DAY, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER HAD. «16. VINCENZO FALCO, ed | Arienzo | PASQUALE, e CHIARA RIVETTI | A 15 OTTOBRE 1814» ed «ANDREANA CRISCI | Arienzo | ARCANGELO, e SARA RUGGIERO». The households row for this marriage has carried an em-dash in the date column since the archive began; the parish act («Vincentium Falco filium Paschalis, e Clarae Rivetta, e Andreanam Crisci filiam Arcangeli, e [Rosae] Ruggiero») gives the parties and no day. He was TWENTY-TWO — baptised 1 February 1792 — and she was SEVENTEEN, baptised 30 November 1796

evidence: «ARCANGELO, e SARA RUGGIERO» — SARA, not ROSA. The archive's only previous source for this woman is the parish marriage act, whose machine transcript gives «e [ROSAE] Ruggiero» WITH THE FORENAME IN BRACKETS, the archive's own mark for a reading it did not trust. The civil index is unambiguous. AND IT EXPLAINS A NAME: the daughter born to this couple on 19 DECEMBER 1828 was called SARA — the only Sara in the household, and this archive found her only yesterday. She was named for her mother's mother. The midwife who declared that birth was GELSOMINA RUGGIERO, sixty, and a Gelsomina Ruggiero stood MATRINA at this couple's son Raffaele's baptism in 1818; the Ruggiero kinship is now MORE likely and is STILL NOT CLAIMED

evidence: READ FROM THE IMAGE AT LAST, and the machine transcript was right. «Anno Domini 1841 die vero 27. NOVEMBRIS obiit JOANNES FALCO filius JOSEPHI et ANTONIAE DI GUIDA, aetate sua ANNORUM 24 CIRCITER, omnibus Sacramentis munitus et in commendatione animae adjutus, cujus cadaver IN SODALITATE S. MARIAE GRATIARUM jacet» — the margin gives the Italian form, GIOVANNI FALCO. THE «24 CIRCITER» IS CONFIRMED, so this man was born about 1817 and CANNOT be DON GIOVANNI FALCO the deacon, whose birth of 6 April 1825 is fixed by his civil act AND his parish baptism and who died in 1849. THIS HOUSEHOLD HAD TWO LIVING SONS NAMED GIOVANNI between 1825 and 1841, which the archive's necronym rule does not explain: the elder was alive when the younger was named. HE DIED FORTIFIED WITH ALL THE SACRAMENTS, which the register does not say of everyone. AND THERE IS NO CIVIL DEATH ACT FOR HIM — all ninety acts of the Arienzo 1841 death register were read on 14 September 2026 and hold no Falco at all

evidence: «cujus cadaver IN SODALITATE S[ANCTAE] MARIAE GRATIARUM jacet» — the CONFRATERNITY OF SANTA MARIA DELLE GRAZIE. THE SAME BURIAL PLACE recorded for «FRANCISCA CRISCI, VIDUA […] FALCO» on 31 December 1805, the woman who may be the founder's wife and whose identification is an open question here. A confraternity buried many families and this is NOT offered as evidence of kinship; it is recorded because the archive holds only two burials with a named place and both are in this one

«…è morto nella sua propria casa DON GIOVANNI FALCO, nato in Arienzo, di anni VENTICINQUE, di professione DIACONO … figlio di GIUSEPPE FALCO di professione COLONO … e di ANTONIA DI GUIDA» — 26 November 1849, ore ventidue. THE ONLY MAN IN THIS FAMILY KNOWN TO HAVE TAKEN ORDERS, from a household of contadini on strada Camellara. Born 6 April 1825 by both his civil act and his parish baptism, so he was TWENTY-FOUR YEARS AND SEVEN MONTHS, and the act rounds it to twenty-five. NOT the Giovanni Falco of this house who was buried on 27 November 1841 «annorum 24 circiter» — two brothers of one name, alive together for sixteen years. The declarants are GENNARO CIOFFI, 52, and FRANCESCO CIOFFI, 56, both contadini of strada Camellara. The act also keeps GIUSEPPE FALCO ALIVE in November 1849 at about seventy, with no «fu» before his name. ADDED TO THE HOUSEHOLD FILE 15 Sep 2026: the act was read from the image on 13 September and had lived only in this archive's corrections log since

evidence: A FOURTH CHILD FOR THE FIRST-COUSIN MARRIAGE, and the third of them to die small. «71. FALCO PASQUALE | Arienzo | contadino | FALCO FRANCESCO, e FALCO RAFFAELA | A 30 detto [OTTOBRE] 1838» — the row above it is dated 10 Ottobre, which fixes the month. This household is FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO, son of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti, and RAFFAELA FALCO, daughter of Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida — first cousins, married 16 July 1832. Their children now run CARMINA (d. 19 Dec 1832), PASQUALINA (d. 14 Sep 1836), PASQUALE (d. 30 Oct 1838) and CLEMENTE (d. 14 Aug 1853). FROM THE INDEX, NOT THE ACT: atto 71 has not been read, and no age is recorded here

evidence: A THIRD CHILD, and the first of this house who is not called Anna. «55. FALCO MATTEO | Arienzo | contadino | FALCO MICHELE, e VIGLIOTTA ANTONIA | 24 detto [AGOSTO] 1842». THE FORENAMES ARE SHORTENED, which this register does constantly: the household head is MICHELANGELO FALCO, son of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti, and his wife is MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA — her surname is the distinctive half and it matches. THE ARCHIVE DOES NOT CLAIM THIS ABSOLUTELY: a separate «Michele Falco» married to an Antonia is not impossible at Arienzo, and only the act itself would settle it. His two sisters, both called ANNA, died in 1831 and 1834. FROM THE INDEX, NOT THE ACT

evidence: A CONFLICT, PUBLISHED AS ONE. The 1832 death index reads «14. MORGILLO RAFFAELA | Arienzo | contadina | MORGILLO CARLANTONIO, e FALCO ROSA | A 9 MARZO 1832». This archive already holds, from the act, «RAFFAELE MORGILLO, 22, CONTADINO, figlio di Carlantonio Morgillo», died 9 MAY 1832. SAME DAY OF THE MONTH, DIFFERENT MONTH, DIFFERENT ENDING, DIFFERENT SEX. Either this couple lost two children nine weeks apart, or one record has been read two ways — «Marzo» and «Maggio» begin alike, and so do «Raffaela» and «Raffaele». THE ACT IS THE STRONGER SOURCE for the age and the trade; the index is a clerk's copy. NOT RESOLVED: reading atto 14 of 1832 and comparing it with the act already held would settle it in one pass

evidence: A FOURTH CHILD. «55. FALCO CARMELA | Arienzo | contad[ina] | MICHELE, e VIGLIATO ANT[ONI]A | 4 AGOSTO [1859]». THE SAME SHORTENING AS THE 1842 ACT AND THE SAME CAUTION: the head of this house is MICHELANGELO FALCO and his wife MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA, and the index gives both forenames clipped. VIGLIOTTA — here written VIGLIATO — is the half that identifies. A separate Michele Falco married to an Antonia is not impossible, and only the act settles it. Her siblings are two ANNA (d. 1831, d. 1834) and MATTEO (d. 1842)

evidence: SHE LIVED, AND SHE MARRIED. Found in the 1828 tavola three days ago and known only as a birth, Sara Falco is the bride of «ATTO DI SOLENNE PROMESSA DI MATRIMONIO, Num. d'ordine 6», 14 FEBRUARY 1855 at sixteen hours, before CARLO CARFORA, sindaco of Arienzo: «…sono comparsi nella Casa Comunale ANTONIO MAURO MAGGIORE, nato in ARIENZO, di professione FRUTTAJOLO, domiciliato STRADA CROCE, figlio di DOMENICO di professione simile … e di VINCENZA GROSSO … e SARA FALCO MAGGIORE, nata in ARIENZO, domiciliata STRADA CAMELLARA, figlia di VINCENZO di professione COLONO … e di ANDREANA…». THE MARGIN CERTIFIES THE CHURCH: the parroco of Sant'Andrea returned the certificate for the celebration on the FIFTEENTH of February. She was TWENTY-SIX, born 19 December 1828 — and her father is a COLONO here where every earlier act makes him a contadino
